name: DART
first: First demonstration of kinetic-impactor planetary defense; first time humans moved an asteroid
description: DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) was the first planetary-defense mission ever flown — a 611-kg spacecraft sent to hit a 160-m asteroid hard enough to change its orbit. The target was Dimorphos, a moonlet of the 780-m asteroid Didymos. Launched 2021-11-24 on a Falcon 9; the SMART Nav autonomous navigation system took over 4 hours before impact to distinguish Dimorphos from its parent and target the smaller body. Impact 2022-09-26 at 23:14 UTC at 6.14 km/s. Measured orbital-period change: 33 minutes (4.2%), exceeding the 73-second success threshold by ~25×. Momentum-transfer enhancement factor β ≈ 3.6 indicated significant carry from ejected surface material. The CubeSat LICIACube observed the plume; HST and JWST imaged the resulting ejecta tail for weeks. First demonstration that humans can move an asteroid.

events.label: IMPACT
events.note: 23:14 UTC. 6.14 km/s. 33-min orbital-period change — first deflection of an asteroid by humans.
